answer.rationale: The low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the 18% mandate. Memory_c2 records that the previous switch to that same vendor was operationally clean — quick onboarding, accurate invoicing. Memory_c3 records that a dual-source arrangement protected the line through an earlier shortage; switching primary supply without retaining the incumbent as a fallback would re-create the single-point-of-failure that c3 eliminated. Because I can execute only one decision this cycle, I will issue the switch to the low-cost vendor as primary but explicitly retain the incumbent on a month-to-month bridging arrangement (analogous to the deferral mechanism in c5) so that the assembly line running at 94% with zero buffer is not exposed to a single-source gap during the transition window. Negotiation (c4) and multi-year pricing (c6) are deferred to next cycle once the new price baseline is locked in.
